Council Minutes  1  09/18/2023
   CEREMONIAL MATTERS Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring October 2023 as
  "First Tee-Greater Pasadena Month," in the City of Pasadena. Kaleb

r  Gleason, First Tee Board Member, expressed appreciation and
  gratitude to the Rose Bowl Operating Company and City Council for
  their support, and spoke on the community benefits provided by First
  Tee - Greater Pasadena.

  The Mayor spoke on the passing of Governor Bill Richardson, a two-
  term Democratic governor of New Mexico, and American Ambassador
  to the United Nations, who was born in Pasadena, and stated that the
  City Council will adjourn in his memory.

  PUBLIC COMMENT ON  Briza Silva, Blair Middle School student, advocated for the City
  MATTERS NOT ON THE  Council's assistance in repairing the air conditioning system at Blair
  AGENDA  Middle School gym, stating that the extreme heat is causing the
  students to become ill.

  The following individuals advocated for the City Council to take urgent
  action to protect Pasadena residents from heat-related climate
  change, advocated for the City to achieve its stated goal of carbon free
  energy by 2030 and/or provided comments related to climate change:

  Adrian Velazquez, Pasadena resident
  Rachel Burcham, Pasadena resident

[]  Wen Lee, Pasadena resident
  Robert Haw, representing Transition Pasadena
  Oliva Tan, representing Pasadena 100
  Paula Hu, Arcadia resident
  Una Jost, Pasadena resident
  Christy Zamani, Pasadena resident

  The following individuals advocated for amending the City Charter to
  incorporate bodycam footage and other video sources as part of the
  investigative process for critical incidents involving the Pasadena
  Police Department.

  Alien Shay, Pasadena resident
  Olden Denham, Pasadena resident

  Burke Farrar, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns regarding the
  City's adopted ordinance related to time limitations on development
  projects; and advocated for the City Council to amend the ordinance
  to allow extensions to be applied to all projects in the City.

  Michell Martin, Pasadena resident, requested assistance with her

L  rental property management company, as the company is not abiding
  by the City's recent Charter Amendment Measure - the Pasadena Fair
  and Equitable Housing Charter Amendment.

  Council Minutes  2  09/18/2023
   Adriana Bautista, representing Black Lives Matter, expressed
  concerns with the allegations and complaints towards several
  members of Pasadena Police Department (PPD) and leadership
  related to alleged illegal and unethical activities within the PPD.

  Councilmember Hampton asked the City Manager to follow up with the
  Pasadena Unified School District staff regarding the repair issue for
  the air conditioning system at Blair Middle School gymnasium.

  Vice Mayor Williams asked staff to ensure Ms. Martin is provided with
  contact information to the Housing Rights Center, and the Pasadena
  Rental Housing Board.

   (2) Establish the Scope and Charge for a Charter Study Task Force

r  (3) Provide direction to staff on Technical Charter Amendment

  City Clerk Jomsky presented a Powerpoint reviewing staff's cover
  memo, the potential Charter Study scope and charge, and citing
  information from the final report of the City's 1998 Charter Reform
  Task Force; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Rivas supported the topic list/scope detailed in the
  cover memo, clarifying that the issue of City Council compensation be
  reviewed broadly, including possible enhancements to include
  childcare expenses, but emphasized that she is not advocating for full-
  time compensated positions; and incorporating a discussion on
  campaign contribution limits, recognizing this may be done by
  ordinance or Charter Amendment:

  Councilmember Hampton advocated for the Charter Study Task Force
  to study the Community Police Oversight Committee's (CPOC) scope
  related to its authority and duties as an added topic to the list of City
  governance issues. He stated he is not supportive of the term limits
  discussion, but he believes the Task Force may organically discuss
  the issue of term limits. Councilmember Hampton echoed support for
  the Task Force reviewing the City Council's compensation taking into
  consideration childcare expenses.

  Vice Mayor Williams advocated for the Task Force to study Article
  XVIII (the Pasadena Fair and Equitable Housing Charter Amendment)
  and determine how to improve the measure. In addition, she asked
  that the City Council's compensation review include "family care" (or
  eldercare) as opposed to just "childcare."

  Councilmember Masuda reiterated his request that the Task Force
  study the issue related to a vacancy occurring in the office of the
  Mayor, noting it should be the City Council that appoints a Mayor to
  serve, and not just automatically fall to the Vice Mayor to serve as
  Mayor (as is currently the requirement stated in the City Charter).

  City Clerk Jomsky agreed to amend the topic to incorporate
  Councilmember Masuda's concerns, under the Vacancy Appointment
  Process for Mayor and City Council - Consider options for allowing
  Special Elections, and review the Charter requirements pertaining to
  a vacancy in the office of the Mayor as it relates to the Vice Mayor
  position.

  Councilmember Lyon stated his support for the proposed review of the
  City Council compensation as an equity issue, and how to make
  Councilmember positions accessible/attainable to more people. In

  Council Minutes  9  09/18/2023
   addition, he noted his strong preference to not study Article XVIII at
  this time, as he believes the Pasadena Rental Housing Board (PRHB)
  is just getting up to speed in its work, and it is too soon for the City to
  initiate a substantive review of those provisions. With regard to
  CPOC's authority, Councilmember Lyon stated that prior to a Task
  Force review, he would prefer the CPOC conduct its own review of
  their authority and how it compares to other jurisdictions.

  Mayor Gordo expressed concerns with changing/affecting the City's
  current form of government related to police oversight but supported
  having the CPOC conduct a self-review including examining best-in-
  class models of police oversight occurring in other jurisdictions.

  Councilmember Madison spoke in support of setting the Task Force's
  scope of work and charge, as follows:

  Scope

  > Vacancy Appointment Process for Mayor and City Council -
  Consider options for allowing Special Elections, and review the
  Charter requirements pertaining to a vacancy in the office of
  the Mayor as it relates to the Vice Mayor position
  > Mayor and City Council Term Limits
  > Review of Timing of Mayoral Election
  > Review of Vice Mayor Appointment Process, Timing, and/or
  Length of Term
  > City Council compensation, broadly, as well as dedicated
  childcare and eldercare allowances for members of the City
  Council
  > Campaign contribution limits

  Charge

  > Study and fully examine topics submitted by City Council to
  Task Force;
  > Provide recommendations on those topics, including whether
  to amend the City Charter, as part of a Final Report submitted
  to the City Council by May/June 2024;
  > Provide recommended City Charter amendments in a priority
  topics list, keeping in mind the number of ballot measures that
  might create voter fatigue issues;
  > Provide recommended ballot question(s) for Charter
  amendments); and
  > Provide recommended changes/amendments/additions to City
  Charter text.
n
